def odd_position(lst):
    """
    Checks whether every element at an odd index (1st, 3rd, etc. in 0-based indexing) 
    contains an odd number.
    
    Note: In standard programming contexts involving "odd positions", we usually refer to 
    indices that are themselves odd numbers (i.e., index 1, 3, 5...). 
    
    If the requirement meant "elements at even indices" or a different definition of position,
    this function would need adjustment. Based on the assertion provided:
    
        lst = [2, 1, 4, 3, 6, 7, 6, 3]
        Indices:   0  1  2  3  4  5  6  7
        
        Odd indices are: 1 (value 1), 3 (value 3), 5 (value 7), 7 (value 3).
        All these values (1, 3, 7, 3) are odd numbers. Hence returns True.

    :param lst: List of integers
    :return: Boolean indicating if all elements at odd indices are odd numbers
    """
    
    # Iterate through the list with index and value
    for i in range(len(lst)):
        # Check only odd indices (1, 3, 5...)
        if i % 2 != 0: 
            # If an element is found at an odd index that is NOT odd itself
            if lst[i] % 2 == 0:
                return False
                
    return True

# Test the function with the provided assertion
if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert odd_position([2,1,4,3,6,7,6,3]) == True
    print("Assertion passed!")
